lessons.title: Découvrir les mots
lessons.oneGoal: Students recognize that French has words we can discover and explore

opening.activity: Welcome circle - Show magnifying glass and say 'Nous sommes des explorateurs!' Use TPR to mime looking and discovering. Point to French words around the room.
opening.visualSupports: Visual schedule showing lesson flow, Word detective poster with magnifying glass image

decisionPoints.moment: If students are very excited about exploring
decisionPoints.choice: Extend the room tour by 2 minutes or channel energy into discovery game

decisionPoints.moment: If some students seem hesitant to participate
decisionPoints.choice: Start with familiar English words first, then transition to French

main.activity: Word Detective Walk - Take students around the room to 'discover' French words on labels, posters, books. Students point and teacher names each word clearly. Create a simple chart of discovered words with pictures.
materials: Simple picture cards for common words
main.visualSupports: Word discovery chart with pictures, Visual instructions for word hunt

decisionPoints.moment: If students find many words quickly
decisionPoints.choice: Add categorizing activity (colors, animals, etc.) or extend to hallway hunt

decisionPoints.moment: If students struggle to find words
decisionPoints.choice: Guide them to specific locations or provide picture clues for word matching

decisionPoints.moment: If chart becomes too full
decisionPoints.choice: Create multiple charts by category or focus on 5-7 most interesting words

closing.activity: Circle back - Show three discovered words with pictures. Students repeat after teacher. End with 'Nous sommes des explorateurs de mots!'
closing.visualSupports: Three chosen words with clear pictures, Class motto poster

decisionPoints.moment: If students want to share more words
decisionPoints.choice: Allow 1-2 additional shares or promise to continue tomorrow

decisionPoints.moment: If energy is low at closing
decisionPoints.choice: Add action chant or celebration dance with the motto

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students having difficulty distinguishing French from English words
troubleshooting.then: Use more visual supports, point to mouth when saying French sounds, use familiar cognates first

lessons.realWorldConnection: People use words to communicate every day in French - in stores, on signs, in conversations

forStruggling: Allow pointing instead of verbal responses
forAdvanced: Find words that start with same sound
forELL: Connect to home language cognates when possible
Use extra visual and gesture supports
Allow code-switching during discovery
Pair with bilingual buddy

observable: Points to French words when directed
checkpoints: Can they identify that French has words we can explore?
Do they show engagement with the exploration concept?
Are they beginning to distinguish French sounds?

lessons.title: Sons et lettres
lessons.oneGoal: Students connect French sounds to letters they can see

opening.activity: Review yesterday's discovered words from chart. Point to each word and have students repeat the sounds they hear.
opening.visualSupports: Yesterday's word discovery chart, Sound symbols poster, Listening ear visual cue

decisionPoints.moment: If students remember many words from yesterday
decisionPoints.choice: Spend extra time on sound exploration or move faster to new activity

decisionPoints.moment: If students need more review of discovered words
decisionPoints.choice: Add picture matching or extend review with actions

main.activity: Sound Matching Game - Show large letter cards A, E, I, O, U. Say simple French words (ami, eau, etc.) and students listen for the vowel sounds. Use picture cards to support meaning. Students move to the letter they hear.
materials: Small vowel cards for each student
main.visualSupports: Vowel sound posters with mouth positions, Picture-word cards, Floor letter spaces marked clearly

decisionPoints.moment: If students master vowel identification quickly
decisionPoints.choice: Add consonant sounds (M, P, T) or increase word complexity

decisionPoints.moment: If movement becomes too chaotic
decisionPoints.choice: Switch to seated pointing activity or smaller groups

decisionPoints.moment: If students struggle with sound isolation
decisionPoints.choice: Exaggerate mouth movements, slow down speech, add visual cues

closing.activity: Sound Circle - Everyone sits and practices the 5 vowel sounds with hand gestures: A (arms wide), E (hands by ears), I (point up), O (make circle), U (pucker lips).
closing.visualSupports: Gesture poster for each vowel sound, Sound-symbol connections chart

decisionPoints.moment: If students want to repeat gestures many times
decisionPoints.choice: Make it into a fun rhythm or song, or save energy for tomorrow

movementBreaks: All vowel gestures with full body movement

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students confusing French vowel sounds with English ones
troubleshooting.then: Use mouth position mirrors, slow down pronunciation, emphasize physical gestures

lessons.realWorldConnection: Reading signs, labels, and books requires knowing letter sounds - like the letters on the bathroom doors or lunch menu

forStruggling: Use extra visual mouth position cues
forAdvanced: Find multiple words with same vowel
forELL: Compare to home language vowel sounds
Use extra gesture and visual supports
Allow native language sound approximations
Practice with familiar English cognates first
forIEP: Provide sensory supports for sound work

observable: Attempts to imitate French vowel sounds
checkpoints: Can they hear differences between vowel sounds?
Do they attempt to match sounds to letters?
Are they engaging with phonetic exploration?

lessons.title: Familles de sons
lessons.oneGoal: Students group words that start with the same sound

opening.activity: Sound Review - Practice vowel sounds from yesterday with gestures. Then show family photo and explain 'famille' - people who belong together.
opening.visualSupports: Vowel sound poster, Family concept visual showing people grouped together

decisionPoints.moment: If students want to share about their own families
decisionPoints.choice: Allow 2-3 brief shares or save family discussion for social studies

decisionPoints.moment: If vowel review takes longer than expected
decisionPoints.choice: Quick review of 3 vowels only or extend by 2 minutes

movementBreaks: Pointing to family members in photo

main.activity: Sound Family Sorting - Give students picture cards (ballon, bébé, bateau / chat, chien, chaussure / pain, papa, poisson). Students sort cards by beginning sound into labeled circles. Teacher models first few.
materials: Picture cards for B, CH, P sounds (6-8 per family, 5-6 sets)
Sorting circles or hula hoops (3 per group)
main.visualSupports: Sound family house posters, Sorting demonstration chart, Picture-word connection cards

decisionPoints.moment: If students sort quickly and accurately
decisionPoints.choice: Add more sound families (M, T) or have them create new categories

decisionPoints.moment: If students struggle with sound discrimination
decisionPoints.choice: Focus on 2 families only, exaggerate beginning sounds, use more modeling

decisionPoints.moment: If cards get mixed up or lost
decisionPoints.choice: Switch to whole-group sorting or use larger demo cards

closing.activity: Family Parade - Each sound family group stands up and says their sound together, then marches around showing their pictures.
materials: Optional: simple musical instrument for marching
closing.visualSupports: Sound family banners or signs, Marching route visual

decisionPoints.moment: If students are very energetic about parading
decisionPoints.choice: Extend parade or channel energy into organized chanting

decisionPoints.moment: If some students don't want to march
decisionPoints.choice: Allow seated participation or assign as 'parade watchers'

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students mixing up similar beginning sounds (B/P, CH sounds)
troubleshooting.then: Use mouth position mirrors, practice sounds in isolation, use stronger visual contrasts

lessons.realWorldConnection: Grouping similar things helps us organize our thoughts and learning - like putting all the books together or all the toys together

forStruggling: Focus on most distinct sounds (B vs M)
forAdvanced: Find objects in room for each family
forELL: Connect to similar sounds in home language
Use extra visual cues and gestures
Allow sorting with home language words
Provide one-on-one sound practice
forIEP: Use larger materials for easier manipulation

checkpoints: Can they hear when words start with the same sound?
Do they understand the concept of sound families?
Are they beginning to categorize by phonetic features?

lessons.title: Jeu des rimes
lessons.oneGoal: Students recognize words that sound similar at the end (rhymes)

opening.activity: Review sound families from yesterday by having students make the B, P, and CH sounds. Explain that today we listen to the END of words.
opening.visualSupports: Sound family poster, Visual showing word beginning vs. ending, Listening ear pointing to end

decisionPoints.moment: If students want to continue with beginning sounds
decisionPoints.choice: Quick game with beginning sounds or emphasize transition to endings

decisionPoints.moment: If concept of 'end' seems unclear
decisionPoints.choice: Use physical demonstrations (end of line, end of book) or extend explanation

movementBreaks: Making B, P, CH sounds with gestures

main.activity: Rhyme Time - Teach simple rhyme 'Chat, rat, chocolat!' with rhythm sticks. Show picture cards that rhyme (chat/rat, pain/main, eau/bateau). Students clap when they hear rhyming words.
main.visualSupports: Rhyming word pairs poster, Rhythm pattern chart, Visual cue for clapping timing

decisionPoints.moment: If students catch onto rhyming quickly
decisionPoints.choice: Add more rhyme pairs or let students suggest their own rhymes

decisionPoints.moment: If rhythm sticks become distracting
decisionPoints.choice: Switch to hand clapping or collect instruments

decisionPoints.moment: If students struggle to hear rhymes
decisionPoints.choice: Exaggerate ending sounds, slow down, use fewer examples

movementBreaks: Standing to act out rhyming words

closing.activity: Rhyme Circle - Students sit in circle and pass a ball. When they catch it, they say one word from today's rhymes and everyone else says the rhyming partner.
closing.visualSupports: Circle sitting arrangement visual, Rhyme pairs reference chart, Turn-taking cues

decisionPoints.moment: If some students can't remember rhyme partners
decisionPoints.choice: Provide visual cues or allow peers to help

decisionPoints.moment: If ball passing becomes chaotic
decisionPoints.choice: Switch to pointing/calling names or teacher-controlled passing

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students having difficulty hearing rhyming endings
troubleshooting.then: Slow down speech, exaggerate endings, use visual mouth cues, try with English rhymes first

lessons.realWorldConnection: Rhymes help us remember songs, poems, and make language fun - like the songs we sing or the books we enjoy

forAdvanced: Create new rhymes with given words
Find rhymes beyond the lesson examples
Help teach rhyming concept to peers
forELL: Connect to rhymes in home language
Use familiar English rhymes as bridge
Extra visual and gestural supports
Allow approximate rhyming attempts
forIEP: Focus on rhythm rather than exact rhymes

checkpoints: Can they identify rhyming word pairs?
Do they understand that rhymes sound similar at the end?
Are they developing phonological awareness?

lessons.title: Mots courts et longs
lessons.oneGoal: Students compare and categorize words by their length

opening.activity: Practice rhyming from yesterday with 'Chat, rat, chocolat!' Then show arms for 'court' (close together) and 'long' (far apart).
opening.visualSupports: Short vs long comparison poster, Arm gesture demonstration chart, Rhyme reminder cards

decisionPoints.moment: If students want to continue rhyming games
decisionPoints.choice: Quick rhyme round or transition with rhyming short/long words

decisionPoints.moment: If short/long concept needs more demonstration
decisionPoints.choice: Use classroom objects or extend physical demonstrations

main.activity: Word Measuring - Show word cards (la, éléphant, chat, ordinateur). Students use arms or fingers to show if words are 'court' or 'long'. Sort cards into two boxes labeled with visual symbols.
materials: Word cards with varied lengths (30-40 cards)
main.visualSupports: Word length comparison chart, Sorting box labels with symbols, Finger-counting guide

decisionPoints.moment: If students categorize accurately and quickly
decisionPoints.choice: Add more challenging words or introduce syllable counting

decisionPoints.moment: If students disagree on word length
decisionPoints.choice: Demonstrate syllable clapping or use visual letter counting

decisionPoints.moment: If sorting becomes disorganized
decisionPoints.choice: Switch to whole-group sorting or use floor sorting areas

movementBreaks: Acting out long and short with whole body

closing.activity: Length Line-up - Students stand and arrange themselves in order from shortest to longest names, with teacher support for pronunciation.
closing.visualSupports: Length ordering example, Name length comparison chart, Visual line-up guide

decisionPoints.moment: If students struggle with name ordering
decisionPoints.choice: Use name cards or simplify to just short vs long groups

decisionPoints.moment: If line-up is successful quickly
decisionPoints.choice: Try ordering other classroom words or extend to syllable discussion

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students inconsistent in judging word length (letters vs syllables vs sounds)
troubleshooting.then: Demonstrate multiple ways to measure - visual letters, clapped syllables, finger counting

lessons.realWorldConnection: Long and short words appear in books, signs, and everyday writing - like short words on stop signs and long words on street signs

forStruggling: Work with 2-3 examples at a time
forAdvanced: Find patterns in long vs short words
Help explain length concept to peers
forELL: Use familiar words from home language for comparison
Extra visual supports for length concept
Allow approximate length judgments
Connect to English word length patterns

observable: Distinguishes between short and long words
Uses appropriate gestures for word length
checkpoints: Can they identify which words are longer or shorter?
Do they understand the concept of measuring words?
Are they developing word awareness skills?

lessons.title: Syllabes et battements
lessons.oneGoal: Students identify syllables by clapping word parts

opening.activity: Review long and short words with arm gestures. Introduce clapping by clapping your name slowly: 'Ma-da-me Smith' (3 claps).
opening.visualSupports: Syllable clapping demonstration poster, Name broken into parts visually

decisionPoints.moment: If students immediately understand clapping concept
decisionPoints.choice: Move quickly to name activity or add more complex examples

main.activity: Name Clapping Circle - Students sit in circle with instruments. Each student claps their name syllables and everyone repeats. Then try picture words: 'é-lé-phant', 'chat', 'cho-co-lat'.
main.visualSupports: Circle arrangement guide, Syllable counting visual aids, Picture-word syllable charts

decisionPoints.moment: If instruments become too distracting
decisionPoints.choice: Switch to hand clapping or collect instruments for focus time

decisionPoints.moment: If students struggle with syllable identification
decisionPoints.choice: Use chin-tapping method or slow down demonstration

closing.activity: Syllable Symphony - Whole class claps 'Au re-voir' (3 claps) together to end the lesson.
closing.visualSupports: 'Au re-voir' broken into syllables visually, Conductor gestures guide

decisionPoints.moment: If students want to try other goodbye phrases
decisionPoints.choice: Try 'À bientôt' or stick with practiced phrase for success

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students clapping too fast or not matching syllable breaks
troubleshooting.then: Use slower demonstration, try chin-tapping method, use visual syllable breaks

lessons.realWorldConnection: Breaking words into parts helps us read and spell new words - like when we sound out unfamiliar words in books

forStruggling: Use physical chin support for syllables
forELL: Connect to rhythm patterns in home language
Use familiar words for practice
Allow approximate syllable identification
Focus on rhythm rather than perfect counting
forIEP: Modify clapping expectations (allow any rhythm participation)
Focus on participation rather than accuracy

checkpoints: Can they hear separate syllables in words?
Do they understand that words have parts?
Are they developing phonological awareness through rhythm?

lessons.title: Petits mots magiques
lessons.oneGoal: Students recognize high-frequency words that appear everywhere

opening.activity: Practice syllable clapping with 'Bon-jour' and 'Au re-voir'. Show magic wand and explain these are 'mots magiques' that appear everywhere.
opening.visualSupports: Magic words concept poster with stars, Syllable breakdown cards from lesson 6

decisionPoints.moment: If students are very excited about magic theme
decisionPoints.choice: Extend magic introduction or channel enthusiasm into word hunt

main.activity: Magic Word Hunt - Show 3 high-frequency words (le, la, et) on large cards. Look through simple French books together to find these 'magic words'. Students point and count how many times they appear.
materials: Large magic word cards (le, la, et)
main.visualSupports: High-frequency word poster, Counting tally chart, Magic word reference cards

decisionPoints.moment: If students find words very quickly
decisionPoints.choice: Add more magic words (un, une, je) or extend hunt to classroom environment

decisionPoints.moment: If students struggle to locate words in text
decisionPoints.choice: Use larger text books or guide them to specific pages with many examples

movementBreaks: Pointing and reaching to find words

closing.activity: Magic Word Spell - Students stand and 'cast spells' by saying each magic word while waving imaginary wands: 'le!', 'la!', 'et!'
materials: Optional: craft stick wands for each student
closing.visualSupports: Spell-casting gesture guide, Magic words with visual cues

decisionPoints.moment: If students want to create more magic spells
decisionPoints.choice: Allow creative spell variations or focus on the three target words

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students confusing 'le' and 'la' or not recognizing these small words
troubleshooting.then: Use color coding, practice in isolation, point out word shapes and patterns

lessons.realWorldConnection: These 'magic words' help us read books, signs, and messages faster - they're like keys that unlock reading

forStruggling: Focus on one magic word at a time
Use finger tracking for word recognition
forAdvanced: Count total occurrences across multiple books
Help teach recognition strategies to peers
forELL: Connect to similar function words in English
Use visual word shapes and patterns
Allow bilingual word recognition strategies
Practice with familiar simple texts
forIEP: Use larger text or different materials
Focus on engagement rather than accuracy

observable: Points to target words when found
checkpoints: Can they identify the three magic words?
Do they understand these words appear frequently?
Are they developing sight word recognition?

lessons.title: Construire des mots
lessons.oneGoal: Students build new words by combining letters and sounds

opening.activity: Review magic words 'le', 'la', 'et' by having students spot them on the word wall. Show letter tiles and explain we're going to BUILD words like construction workers.
opening.visualSupports: Construction worker poster, Word building demonstration chart, Magic words reference

decisionPoints.moment: If students quickly spot all magic words
decisionPoints.choice: Add challenge to find them in books or move quickly to building activity

main.activity: Letter Construction - Give students magnetic letters. Start with simple 3-letter words (pot, ami, eau). Teacher builds first word together, then students try to copy and build new ones with guidance.
materials: Magnetic letters (full alphabet sets for pairs)
main.visualSupports: Word building steps poster, Letter-sound reference chart, Target word picture cards

decisionPoints.moment: If students build words quickly and accurately
decisionPoints.choice: Introduce 4-letter words or let them try free building

decisionPoints.moment: If letter manipulation is difficult
decisionPoints.choice: Use larger letters, focus on 2-letter combinations, or provide more guidance

closing.activity: Word Builders' Show - Students hold up one word they built and say it proudly. Everyone claps for the 'constructors'.
closing.visualSupports: Show and tell format guide, Celebration clapping poster

decisionPoints.moment: If many students want to share multiple words
decisionPoints.choice: Allow extra shares or save additional words for tomorrow's review

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students mixing up letter order or sounds when building
troubleshooting.then: Use step-by-step building guides, practice individual letter sounds, provide visual word patterns

lessons.realWorldConnection: Writers create new words by putting letters and sounds together - just like we do when we write shopping lists or messages

forStruggling: Use picture cues for target words
Allow letter copying rather than independent building
forAdvanced: Help demonstrate building process to peers
forELL: Use familiar words for building practice
Connect to English spelling patterns where helpful
Allow sound approximations
Use extra visual supports for letter-sound connections
forIEP: Use larger letters or different materials
Focus on letter recognition rather than building

checkpoints: Can they combine letters to make recognizable words?
Do they understand that letters create words?
Are they developing beginning spelling awareness?

lessons.title: Mots de la même famille
lessons.oneGoal: Students find words that belong to the same word family

opening.activity: Review word building by having students build 'chat' with letters. Show family photo again and explain word families - words that look and sound similar at the end.
opening.visualSupports: Word families explanation chart, 'Chat' building demonstration, Family connection visual

decisionPoints.moment: If students build 'chat' quickly
decisionPoints.choice: Try building 'rat' immediately or spend more time on family concept explanation

main.activity: Word Family Houses - Set up three 'houses' (sorting mats) for -at, -an, -in families. Students sort word cards (chat, rat, chocolat / plan, Jean, maman / fin, pain, main) into correct family houses.
materials: Three house sorting mats or hula hoops
Word cards for each family (30+ cards total)
main.visualSupports: Word family house posters, Sorting demonstration chart, Picture-word connection cards for difficult vocabulary

decisionPoints.moment: If students sort accurately and quickly
decisionPoints.choice: Add more word families (-et, -on) or have them generate new family members

decisionPoints.moment: If students confuse similar endings
decisionPoints.choice: Focus on two families only or use more distinct ending patterns

closing.activity: Family Reunion - Each word family group stands together and chants their family ending: '-at, -at, we're the -at family!'
materials: Optional: simple instruments for chanting rhythm
closing.visualSupports: Family chant format poster, Ending pattern visual cues

decisionPoints.moment: If students create elaborate chants spontaneously
decisionPoints.choice: Allow creative extensions or focus on the target pattern

movementBreaks: Chanting with full body movement and gestures

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students not hearing or recognizing similar word endings
troubleshooting.then: Exaggerate ending pronunciations, use visual patterns, try with simpler/shorter words

lessons.realWorldConnection: Word families help us predict how to read and spell similar words - like if you know 'cat', you can figure out 'hat' and 'bat'

forStruggling: Work with one word family at a time
Use picture cues for all words
forAdvanced: Find additional words for each family
Try families with different vowel patterns
forELL: Connect to word patterns in home language
Use extra visual and picture supports
Allow discussion of pattern recognition in both languages
Focus on sound patterns over spelling
forIEP: Allow flexible participation in group activities
Celebrate pattern recognition at any level

checkpoints: Can they identify words that end the same way?
Do they understand the word family concept?
Are they recognizing sound and spelling patterns?

lessons.title: Chasse aux mots
lessons.oneGoal: Students search for and identify specific words in text

opening.activity: Review word families by chanting '-at, -an, -in' with actions. Put on detective hats/magnifying glasses and explain we're going hunting for words in real books.
materials: Word family chant cards from lesson 9
opening.visualSupports: Detective poster, Word family reference chart, Hunting/searching visual cues

decisionPoints.moment: If students are very excited about detective role-play
decisionPoints.choice: Extend detective character building or move quickly to text hunting

movementBreaks: Putting on detective gear with drama

main.activity: Text Detective Work - Give pairs of students simple French texts. Have them hunt for previously learned words (le, la, et, words from families). Students circle or highlight words they find and keep count.
main.visualSupports: Target words poster, Detective investigation process chart, Counting/tally visual guides

decisionPoints.moment: If students find target words very easily
decisionPoints.choice: Add more challenging words or extend hunt to classroom environment

decisionPoints.moment: If students struggle to locate words in text
decisionPoints.choice: Use texts with larger print, guide to specific paragraphs, or provide word location clues

movementBreaks: Moving around to work with different pairs

closing.activity: Detective Report - Each pair reports one interesting word they found. Class celebrates all discoveries with detective applause.
closing.visualSupports: Detective report format poster, Celebration applause guide

decisionPoints.moment: If many pairs want to report multiple discoveries
decisionPoints.choice: Allow extended sharing time or save additional reports for tomorrow

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students having difficulty locating specific words within continuous text
troubleshooting.then: Use finger tracking, highlight first letter of target words, use simpler texts with more white space

lessons.realWorldConnection: We search for specific words when reading recipes, instructions, or finding information - like looking for ingredients on a food package

forStruggling: Provide word cards for matching rather than free searching
forAdvanced: Hunt for additional word types (action words, describing words)
Count and compare frequency of different words
Help struggling pairs with their searches
forELL: Use texts with familiar vocabulary
Allow searching for cognates or English-French connections
Provide picture supports for target words
Focus on word recognition over text comprehension
forIEP: Use highlighting instead of circling if easier
Allow verbal reporting of found words
Celebrate any word recognition in text

checkpoints: Can they find target words in continuous text?
Do they understand the concept of word hunting?
Are they developing text scanning skills?

lessons.title: Inventer avec les mots
lessons.oneGoal: Students create simple sentences using their word knowledge

opening.activity: Review word hunting by showing some words they found yesterday. Explain that now we'll put words together to create messages, like building with blocks.
opening.visualSupports: Sentence building concept poster, Building blocks metaphor chart, Found words reference

decisionPoints.moment: If students remember many hunting discoveries
decisionPoints.choice: Use their found words in today's sentences or stick to prepared word cards

main.activity: Sentence Building Workshop - Provide word cards (le, chat, et, petit, grand, la, maison). Students work in pairs to arrange 3-4 words into simple sentences like 'Le chat et la maison'. Teacher circulates to help with word order.
materials: Word card sets for each pair (40-50 cards per set)
main.visualSupports: French sentence pattern poster, Word order guide, Picture-word connection charts

decisionPoints.moment: If students create sentences easily
decisionPoints.choice: Add describing words or encourage longer sentences

decisionPoints.moment: If word order causes confusion
decisionPoints.choice: Provide sentence frames or focus on 2-word combinations first

movementBreaks: Moving word cards around on mats
Standing to share progress with teacher

closing.activity: Sentence Share Circle - Students take turns showing their sentence creations. Class repeats each sentence together.
closing.visualSupports: Sentence sharing format poster, Circle time arrangement visual

decisionPoints.moment: If students create many sentences to share
decisionPoints.choice: Allow multiple shares per pair or save extras for display wall

movementBreaks: Gestures and actions while reading sentences

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students creating word sequences that don't follow French sentence patterns
troubleshooting.then: Model correct patterns repeatedly, use sentence frames, focus on simple subject-verb or noun-adjective patterns

lessons.realWorldConnection: We combine words to share our thoughts, feelings, and ideas with others - like when we tell someone what we want for lunch

forStruggling: Use picture cues for word meaning
forAdvanced: Help explain sentence building to peers
forELL: Compare to English sentence patterns
Use familiar vocabulary in sentences
Allow approximate French word order
Focus on meaning over perfect grammar

checkpoints: Can they create simple word combinations?
Do they understand that words make sentences?
Are they experimenting with French sentence structure?

lessons.title: Mes mots préférés
lessons.oneGoal: Students choose and justify their favorite French words

opening.activity: Review sentence building by having class create one sentence together. Show heart shape and explain everyone has 'mots préférés' - favorite words that they like best.
opening.visualSupports: Favorite words concept poster, Heart shape for preference, Class word collection display

decisionPoints.moment: If class sentence building is very successful
decisionPoints.choice: Create multiple sentences or move to favorites with enthusiasm built up

main.activity: Favorite Word Gallery - Students choose 3 favorite French words from all those learned. They write/draw each word on heart-shaped paper and explain why they like it: 'J'aime... parce que...' (with teacher support).
materials: Word reference charts from all lessons
main.visualSupports: All unit vocabulary displayed, 'J'aime... parce que...' sentence frame, Favorite word examples

decisionPoints.moment: If students struggle to choose only 3 words
decisionPoints.choice: Allow 4-5 favorites or help narrow down with guided questions

decisionPoints.moment: If explanation in French is too challenging
decisionPoints.choice: Allow English explanations or use simple picture reasons

movementBreaks: Moving around to reference word charts

closing.activity: Favorite Word Show-and-Tell - Students share one favorite word and show their heart. Class says 'C'est beau!' after each share.
closing.visualSupports: Show-and-tell format guide, Class response poster

decisionPoints.moment: If many students want to share all their favorites
decisionPoints.choice: Allow extended sharing time or create gallery walk for tomorrow

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students unable to explain why they like certain words
troubleshooting.then: Provide reason prompts (sounds nice, easy to say, funny word, reminds me of...), allow picture explanations

lessons.realWorldConnection: Having favorite words makes reading and writing more personal and enjoyable - like having a favorite song or color

forStruggling: Use picture reasons instead of verbal explanations
Allow teacher scribing for word writing
forAdvanced: Write simple sentences about why they like words
Choose favorites from different word categories
forELL: Allow connection to home language favorites
Use pictures and gestures for explanations
Compare favorite sounds across languages
Support with bilingual word connections
forIEP: Allow alternative ways to show favorites

observable: Selects favorite words from learned vocabulary
Shows personal connection to French vocabulary
checkpoints: Can they identify favorite words from their learning?
Do they show personal connection to French vocabulary?
Are they developing word awareness and preferences?

lessons.title: Dictionnaire d'images
lessons.oneGoal: Students organize their learned words into a visual dictionary

opening.activity: Review favorite words by having a few students share. Show a real dictionary and explain it's a book that organizes all words - we'll make our own with pictures.
opening.visualSupports: Dictionary concept poster, Organization example chart, Picture dictionary sample pages

decisionPoints.moment: If students are fascinated by the real dictionary
decisionPoints.choice: Allow brief exploration time or channel interest into their own dictionary making

main.activity: Dictionary Makers - Students create personal picture dictionaries by sorting their learned words and drawing pictures for each. Start with simple alphabetical order (A words together, B words together, etc.).
materials: Small booklets or folded paper (25 sets)
main.visualSupports: Alphabet organization guide, Picture drawing examples, Dictionary page layout model

decisionPoints.moment: If alphabetical order is too complex
decisionPoints.choice: Organize by themes (animals, actions, etc.) or by lesson sequence

decisionPoints.moment: If students finish their dictionaries quickly
decisionPoints.choice: Add more words or help decorate covers

movementBreaks: Moving around to reference alphabet charts

closing.activity: Dictionary Celebration - Students flip through their dictionaries and share one page they're proud of. Class applauds each mini-dictionary.
closing.visualSupports: Dictionary celebration format, Applause and appreciation cues

decisionPoints.moment: If students want to share multiple pages
decisionPoints.choice: Allow extended sharing or save dictionaries for ongoing reference

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students overwhelming themselves with too many words or struggling with organization
troubleshooting.then: Focus on 5-10 favorite words only, provide pre-made organizing templates, allow theme-based rather than alphabetical organization

lessons.realWorldConnection: Dictionaries help us find and remember words when reading and writing - like when we don't know what a word means in a story

forStruggling: Provide pre-drawn pictures to match with words
forAdvanced: Include word definitions in simple French
Add more vocabulary beyond lesson words
forELL: Include home language translations if desired
Use familiar words as dictionary foundation
Allow creative organization systems
Focus on visual representation over text
forIEP: Modify fine motor expectations for drawing
Focus on word collection rather than perfect organization

observable: Takes pride in personal word collection
checkpoints: Can they organize words in meaningful ways?
Do they understand the purpose of dictionaries?
Are they developing personal vocabulary ownership?

lessons.title: Présentation de mes découvertes
lessons.oneGoal: Students share their word discoveries with classmates

opening.activity: Students get their dictionaries from yesterday. Explain that good explorers share their discoveries with others - like scientists or treasure hunters.
opening.visualSupports: Explorer sharing concept poster, Scientist presentation model, Discovery sharing examples

decisionPoints.moment: If students are eager to share immediately
decisionPoints.choice: Allow quick preview sharing or build anticipation for main activity

main.activity: Word Explorer Presentations - Each student chooses 2-3 words from their dictionary to present to the class. They show the word, picture, and teach it to classmates. Audience repeats each new word.
main.visualSupports: Presentation format guide, Audience participation cues, 'Good presenter' behavior chart

decisionPoints.moment: If presentations take longer than expected
decisionPoints.choice: Allow extended time or continue presentations tomorrow

decisionPoints.moment: If some students are nervous to present
decisionPoints.choice: Allow partner presentations or very brief sharing

closing.activity: Explorer Celebration - Give each presenter a 'Word Explorer' sticker. Class chants 'Nous sommes des explorateurs de mots!' to celebrate everyone's learning journey.
closing.visualSupports: Class motto display, Celebration format guide, Unit learning journey visual

decisionPoints.moment: If students want to continue celebrating discoveries
decisionPoints.choice: Extend celebration or plan future sharing opportunities

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students too nervous to present or struggling to explain their words
troubleshooting.then: Allow partner support, focus on showing pictures rather than explaining, use prompting questions from teacher

lessons.realWorldConnection: Sharing what we learn helps others and strengthens our own understanding - like when we teach our family a new game or skill

forAdvanced: Present more words or create teaching activities
Add explanations about why words are interesting
forELL: Allow explanations in home language if needed
Use visual supports heavily
Focus on pronunciation practice rather than explanation
Celebrate multilingual word knowledge
forIEP: Focus on participation rather than performance

checkpoints: Can they share their word learning with others?
Do they show ownership of their vocabulary development?
Are they building confidence as French learners?

lessons.title: Jeux de mots créatifs
lessons.oneGoal: Students play creative word games for enjoyment and practice

opening.activity: Celebrate completing the core lessons! Explain that now we get to PLAY with all the words we've learned. Show game materials and build excitement.
opening.visualSupports: Game station preview poster, Celebration of learning visual, Word games excitement chart

decisionPoints.moment: Si les élèves sont très excités par l'idée des jeux de mots
decisionPoints.choice: Canaliser l'énergie avec une mini-démonstration ou commencer par un jeu calme

decisionPoints.moment: Si certains élèves semblent inquiets des jeux compétitifs
decisionPoints.choice: Rassurer que tous les jeux sont pour s'amuser ensemble, pas pour gagner

main.activity: Word Game Stations - Set up 3 game stations: 1) Word Bingo with learned words, 2) Musical Words (walk around, when music stops grab a word card), 3) Word Memory matching game. Students rotate every 8 minutes.
main.visualSupports: Station instruction posters, Rotation schedule visual, Game rules charts for each station

decisionPoints.moment: If students want to stay longer at favorite stations
decisionPoints.choice: Allow flexible timing or promise return visits

closing.activity: Game Champions Circle - Everyone sits and shares which game was most fun. Give everyone a 'Word Game Champion' sticker because everyone played well.
closing.visualSupports: Circle sharing format, Game reflection guide, Champion celebration visual

decisionPoints.moment: Si trop d'élèves veulent partager en même temps
decisionPoints.choice: Utiliser le bâton de parole ou limiter à une phrase par élève

decisionPoints.moment: Si un élève n'a pas aimé les jeux
decisionPoints.choice: Valider ses sentiments et demander ce qu'il a préféré dans la leçon

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students getting overwhelmed by game choices or competitive feelings
troubleshooting.then: Simplify to one game at a time, emphasize fun over winning, provide support volunteers for each station

lessons.realWorldConnection: Playing with words makes language learning fun and memorable - like word games families play in the car or at home

forStruggling: Focus on participation rather than game success
forELL: Allow use of familiar words from any language
Pair with bilingual support
Focus on fun rather than perfect French
Use visual game supports
forIEP: Focus on enjoyment of word play

observable: Shows enjoyment of French word activities
checkpoints: Are they enjoying playing with French words?
Do they use learned vocabulary in game contexts?
Are they developing positive associations with French learning?

lessons.title: Histoires avec nos mots
lessons.oneGoal: Students create simple stories using their vocabulary collection

opening.activity: Review favorite word games from yesterday. Show a simple picture book and explain that stories are made with words - we can make stories with OUR words.
opening.visualSupports: Story structure poster (beginning-middle-end), Word collection display, Picture book example

decisionPoints.moment: Si les élèves sont distraits par le livre d'images
decisionPoints.choice: Permettre quelques minutes d'exploration libre avant de commencer l'activité

decisionPoints.moment: Si les élèves ne comprennent pas le concept d'histoire
decisionPoints.choice: Utiliser des exemples familiers comme leurs histoires de famille ou de vacances

main.activity: Mini Story Creators - Students choose 4-5 words from their collection and create a simple story. They can draw pictures and use simple sentences like 'Le chat et le chien...' Template: Beginning, middle, end with pictures.
main.visualSupports: Story template example, Beginning-middle-end visual guide, Sentence starter poster

decisionPoints.moment: If students struggle to create story sequences
decisionPoints.choice: Provide story picture prompts or allow simple word lists with pictures

movementBreaks: Moving around to gather word materials

closing.activity: Story Time Circle - 3-4 volunteers share their mini stories. Class responds with 'C'est une belle histoire!' after each one.
closing.visualSupports: Story time format poster, Audience response guide, Story sharing celebration visual

decisionPoints.moment: Si un élève est trop nerveux pour partager son histoire
decisionPoints.choice: Offrir de la lire avec lui ou permettre de montrer seulement les dessins

decisionPoints.moment: Si une histoire est très longue ou confuse
decisionPoints.choice: Remercier chaleureusement et aider à identifier la partie préférée

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students creating disconnected word lists rather than story sequences
troubleshooting.then: Focus on picture storytelling first, provide simple story frames, allow collaborative story creation

lessons.realWorldConnection: Stories help us share experiences and connect with others - like telling family about our day or sharing favorite memories

forAdvanced: Create longer stories with multiple sentences
forELL: Allow bilingual storytelling
Use familiar story patterns from home culture
Focus on visual storytelling with some French words
Connect to known story structures
forIEP: Focus on creative expression over structure

observable: Creates simple narratives using French vocabulary
Uses learned words in creative contexts
checkpoints: Can they use their vocabulary in creative storytelling?
Do they understand basic story structure?
Are they expressing creativity through French words?

lessons.title: Mots dans notre école
lessons.oneGoal: Students identify and collect French words around the school environment

opening.activity: Share a few mini stories from yesterday. Show school map and explain that our school is FULL of French words - we're going on a word treasure hunt around the building.
opening.visualSupports: School layout visual, Word treasure hunt concept poster, French in our environment examples

decisionPoints.moment: Si les élèves sont très excités par la chasse aux mots
decisionPoints.choice: Établir des règles claires de marche silencieuse avant de quitter la classe

decisionPoints.moment: Si certains élèves ont peur d'explorer l'école
decisionPoints.choice: Rassurer qu'on reste ensemble et visiter les endroits familiers d'abord

main.activity: School Word Safari - Take students on guided walk through school (library, office, cafeteria, gym). Students identify and record French words on signs, posters, labels. Work in pairs with clipboards.
main.visualSupports: Safari collection sheet, Word identification guide, School location map

decisionPoints.moment: If students find more words than expected
decisionPoints.choice: Extend hunt time or focus on most interesting discoveries

movementBreaks: Pointing and reaching to identify words

closing.activity: Safari Debrief - Back in classroom, share the most interesting words found. Create a class list of 'School French Words' on chart paper.
closing.visualSupports: School French words chart, Safari debrief format, Word discovery celebration poster

decisionPoints.moment: Si les élèves ont trouvé beaucoup trop de mots pour tous les partager
decisionPoints.choice: Choisir les 5 plus intéressants ou créer plusieurs affiches par catégorie

decisionPoints.moment: Si un élève n'a trouvé aucun mot pendant la chasse
decisionPoints.choice: L'encourager à partager un endroit qu'il a aimé visiter dans l'école

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students having difficulty distinguishing French words from English in school environment
troubleshooting.then: Focus on obvious French signs, provide guidance on French vs English visual cues, use familiar French words as starting points

lessons.realWorldConnection: French words surround us in our daily environment at school and beyond - on signs, in books, and in conversations

Use visual cues to identify French
forAdvanced: Help identify less obvious French words
forELL: Connect to multilingual signs in school
Focus on universal symbols with French labels
Allow recognition of cognates
Use home language knowledge to identify French
forIEP: Focus on exploration rather than collection

observable: Identifies French words in environmental print
Shows curiosity about French in school environment
checkpoints: Can they recognize French words in their school environment?
Do they show awareness of French around them?
Are they developing environmental print awareness?

lessons.title: Atelier de poésie simple
lessons.oneGoal: Students create simple poems using their favorite words and sounds

opening.activity: Review school words found yesterday. Read a simple French poem or chant with rhythm and rhyme. Explain that poems are special ways to play with words and sounds.
materials: Simple French poem book or chant card
opening.visualSupports: Poetry concept poster, Rhythm and rhyme examples, Simple poem format guide

decisionPoints.moment: Si les élèves ne comprennent pas ce qu'est un poème
decisionPoints.choice: Comparer aux chansons qu'ils connaissent ou aux comptines de maternelle

decisionPoints.moment: Si les élèves veulent réciter le poème plusieurs fois
decisionPoints.choice: Permettre la répétition et ajouter des gestes ou des instruments

main.activity: Young Poets Workshop - Students create simple 4-line poems using rhyming words from their collection. Template: 'Dans l'école je vois... / Dans l'école j'entends...' Encourage rhythm and repetition.
main.visualSupports: Poetry template example, Rhyming words reference, Simple poem structure guide

decisionPoints.moment: If students struggle with rhyming or rhythm
decisionPoints.choice: Focus on repetitive phrases or allow free-form word play

movementBreaks: Moving around to gather word materials

closing.activity: Poetry Café - Students sit in circle and share poems like a coffee shop poetry reading. Soft snaps or finger wiggles for applause after each poem.
closing.visualSupports: Poetry café setup visual, Audience appreciation guide, Poetry sharing format

decisionPoints.moment: Si un élève est trop timide pour lire son poème
decisionPoints.choice: Offrir de le lire ensemble ou permettre à un ami de l'aider

decisionPoints.moment: Si les applaudissements deviennent trop bruyants
decisionPoints.choice: Enseigner les applaudissements silencieux du café (remuer les doigts)

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students feeling pressure to create 'perfect' poems or struggling with French rhyme patterns
troubleshooting.then: Emphasize word play over perfect structure, allow repetition instead of rhymes, focus on rhythm and sound patterns

lessons.realWorldConnection: Poetry helps us express feelings and appreciate the beauty of language - like songs we love or beautiful words that make us happy

Focus on favorite word lists rather than structured poems
forAdvanced: Create longer or more complex poems
forELL: Allow bilingual poetry creation
Use familiar rhythm patterns from home language
Focus on sound play over complex meaning
Connect to cultural poetry traditions
forIEP: Focus on creative enjoyment over structure

Shows appreciation for language sounds and rhythms
checkpoints: Are they experimenting creatively with French words and sounds?

lessons.title: Concours d'orthographe amical
lessons.oneGoal: Students participate in a friendly spelling celebration of learned words

opening.activity: Share a few poems from yesterday's poetry café. Explain that today we celebrate how well we can spell our learned words - like a friendly contest where everyone wins.
opening.visualSupports: Friendly spelling celebration poster, 'Everyone wins' concept visual, Spelling celebration format

decisionPoints.moment: Si les élèves semblent anxieux à propos de l'orthographe
decisionPoints.choice: Rassurer que c'est pour célébrer ce qu'ils savent, pas pour les tester

decisionPoints.moment: Si certains élèves ne veulent pas participer au 'concours'
decisionPoints.choice: Expliquer que c'est un jeu d'équipe où tout le monde s'aide

main.activity: Friendly Spelling Celebration - Divide class into mixed-ability teams. Use learned words for team spelling challenges: letter building, word completion, and oral spelling. Focus on encouragement and team support.
main.visualSupports: Team spelling challenge stations, Encouragement phrases poster, Spelling celebration rules

decisionPoints.moment: If competition becomes too intense or stressful
decisionPoints.choice: Switch to collaborative spelling or emphasize teamwork over competition

closing.activity: Spelling Champions Ceremony - Every student receives a 'Spelling Star' certificate. Celebrate growth and effort rather than perfect spelling.
closing.visualSupports: Spelling champions ceremony format, Growth and effort celebration poster, Certificate presentation visual

decisionPoints.moment: Si un élève se compare négativement aux autres
decisionPoints.choice: Souligner ses progrès personnels et ses efforts pendant l'unité

decisionPoints.moment: Si la cérémonie devient trop longue
decisionPoints.choice: Donner tous les certificats ensemble avec un gros applaudissement

troubleshooting.then: Emphasize effort and improvement, use team support strategies, focus on fun rather than perfection

familyConnections.unitLetter:
Chers parents et familles,

Nous sommes ravis de commencer notre nouvelle unité: "Explorateurs de mots"

Cette unité permettra à votre enfant de:
• Explorer des concepts importants en français
• Développer du vocabulaire en français
• Pratiquer de nouvelles compétences
• Faire des connexions avec la vie quotidienne

Quelques thèmes que nous explorerons:
Découvrir les mots, Sons et lettres, Familles de sons, Jeu des rimes, Mots courts et longs

Comment vous pouvez aider à la maison:
• Demandez à votre enfant de partager ce qu'il/elle a appris
• Pratiquez le nouveau vocabulaire ensemble (voir la liste ci-jointe)
• Essayez les activités suggérées quand vous avez du temps
• Célébrez les efforts et les progrès, pas seulement les résultats

Il est normal et bénéfique que votre enfant mélange les langues à la maison.

N'hésitez pas à me contacter si vous avez des questions ou si vous souhaitez partager des ressources culturelles liées à cette unité.

Merci pour votre soutien continu dans l'apprentissage du français!

Cordialement,
[Nom de l'enseignant(e)]
